newsitem.title: Egypt: Egypt rights group condemns church massacre.
newsitem.headline: Egypt rights group condemns church massacre.

text.p: An Egyptian human rights group on Saturday condemned an attack on a church in southern Egypt in which 10 young Coptic Christians were killed and a newspaper said police had detained 130 people for questioning.

Police suspect the Wednesday massacre, the worst attack on Egypt's Christians in almost a year, was the work of the Moslem militant al-Gama'a al-Islamiya (Islamic Group), which has been fighting since 1992 to turn Egypt into a strict Islamic state.

The government newspaper Akhbar al-Youm said on Saturday the Interior Ministry had identified four gunmen who carried out the massacre in Abu Qurqas town, 240 km (150 miles) south of Cairo. It said police had rounded up 130 people for questioning.
The independent Egyptian Human Rights Organisation (EOHR) expressed its "extreme condemnation and rejection of this horrific crime".

"By all indications it is a base and premeditated crime aimed primarily at shaking security and the ties and harmony between Moslems and Copts, thereby threatening the state's stability," it added in a statement.

EOHR sent a team of researchers to Abu Qurqas shortly after the attack on a youth meeting in a church there on Wednesday evening. The researchers interviewed survivors of the attack and witnesses but none were able to identify the gunmen.
The group urged the authorities to move the wounded to hospitals in Cairo where they could receive better care than in the local state hospital.
Police in southern Egypt suspect the same gunmen who attacked the church also killed three Coptic Christians who were found dead in a southern Egyptian village on Friday, security sources said.
The Moslem Brotherhood, the country's largest political Islamic organistation, said it condemned the "criminal, brute attack".
"We also condemn this irresponsible behaviour that will lead to insecurity," the Brotherhood said in a statement.

The outlawed and influential group has denied government charges that it is a front for violent groups such as the Gama'a, saying it wants to turn Egypt into an Islamic state through non-violent means such as elections.
If the Abu Qurqas killings were carried out by Gama'a it would be the first time Egypt's Moslem militants have attacked inside a church.
Gunmen killed eight Christians in a raid on a farm near the southern city of Assiut in February last year but the motive for that attack was never clear.
The Gama'a has attacked Christians in southern Egypt only sporadically, concentrating attacks on policemen and suspected police informers regardless of religion.
EOHR says 82 Copts have been killed in violent attacks in Egypt since 1992. Copts make up about 10 percent of Egypt's population.
More than 1,000 people have been killed since the Gama'a and other militant organisations began their armed campaign against the Egyptian government in 1992.
